newsitem.title: INDIA: India unveils new five-year imports policy.
newsitem.headline: India unveils new five-year imports policy.

text.p: India, unveiling a new five-year export-import policy, said on Monday it had liberalised the imports of 542 items that were so far subject to government restrictions.
A Commerce Ministry statement said that under its Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) scheme, import duty on capital goods had been cut to 10 percent from 15 percent.

"As part of the move towards further liberalisation and globalisation so as to meet the challenge of global competition, the negative list has been pruned as in the earlier Exim policies," the statement said.

The 542 items lifted off a negative list can now be imported openly or under freely transferable special import licences, the statement saidd. A list of the 542 items would be released later on Monday, officials said.
The restricted list comprises items whose imports are banned, or can be imported only under licences directly awarded by the government to importers.
